Class BaseEntity

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.jpa.entity.BaseEntity
Direct Known Subclasses:
AuditableEntity
@MappedSuperclass public abstract class BaseEntity extends Object
A base class for JPA entities that provides a universally unique identifier (UUID) as a primary key.

This class is intended to be extended by entity classes that require a unique and immutable identifier. It ensures that every entity has a stable identifier upon creation and maintains a version for optimistic locking.

Usage


@Entity
public class User extends BaseEntity {
    private String name;

    protected User() {
    }

    public User(String name) {
        this.name = name;
    }

    public String getName() {
        return name;
    }
}

Key Features

  • Automatically assigns a time-based UUID upon creation.
  • Enforces a non-null ID using Objects.requireNonNull(Object, String).
  • Provides a version field for optimistic locking.
  • Implements equals() and hashCode() based on the unique identifier, read through getId() so Hibernate lazy proxies compare equal to the loaded entity.
  • Does not include a toString() method to allow users full control over string representations.

  • Constructor Details

    • BaseEntity

      protected BaseEntity()
      Default constructor that assigns a time-based UUID to the entity.

      This constructor is required for JPA and ensures that an entity always has a stable identifier upon instantiation. Identifiers come from one shared generator, so they are strictly increasing even for entities created within the same millisecond.

    • BaseEntity

      protected BaseEntity(UUID id)
      Constructs an entity with the given UUID.

      This constructor allows for explicit assignment of the UUID, useful when reconstructing entities from external sources.

      Parameters:
      id - the UUID to be assigned to the entity (must not be null)
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if the provided UUID is null

  • Method Details

    • equals

      public boolean equals(Object o)
      Determines equality based on the entity's unique identifier.

      Two entities are considered equal if they have the same UUID. Since UUIDs are universally unique, collision across different entity types is effectively impossible and represents a design error if it occurs.

      The identifier is read through getId(), never the field, on both sides. A Hibernate lazy proxy is a generated subclass whose own fields are not the entity's state; its getId() returns the real identifier without loading the entity. For the same reason this method is not final (a proxy could not intercept it); subclasses should not override it.

      Overrides:
      equals in class Object
      Parameters:
      o - the object to compare against
      Returns:
      true if both entities have the same UUID, false otherwise

    • hashCode

      public int hashCode()
      Computes a hash code using the entity's unique identifier.

      Returns a stable hash code based on the entity's UUID, or 0 if the ID is null. This ensures consistent behavior even in edge cases where the ID might not be set.

      Overrides:
      hashCode in class Object
      Returns:
      a stable hash code based on the entity's UUID, or 0 if ID is null
